source_text: Ὁρᾶτε μέντοι ὡς καὶ τῷ Ἰσαὰκ τὰ αὐτὰ καὶ τῷ Ἰακὼβ ὑπισχνεῖται. Οὕτω γὰρ λέγει τῷ Ἰσαάκ· Καὶ εὐλογηθήσονται ἐν τῷ σπέρματί σου πάντα τὰ ἔθνη τῆς γῆς · τῷ δὲ Ἰακώβ· Καὶ εὐλογηθήσονται ἐν σοὶ πᾶσαι αἱ φυλαὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ἐν τῷ σπέρματί σου . Οὐκέτι τοῦτο τῷ Ἠσαῦ οὐδὲ τῷ Ῥουβὶμ λέγει οὐδὲ ἄλλῳ τινί, ἀλλ᾿ ἐκείνοις ἐξ ὧν ἔμελλεν ἔσεσθαι κατὰ τὴν οἰκονομίαν τὴν διὰ τῆς παρθένου Μαρίας ὁ Χριστός. Εἴγε δὲ καὶ τὴν εὐλογίαν Ἰούδα καταμάθοις, ἴδοις ἄν ὃ λέγω. Μερίζεται γὰρ τὸ σπέρμα ἐξ Ἰακώβ, καὶ διὰ Ἰούδα καὶ Φαρὲς καὶ Ἰεσσαὶ καὶ Δαυῒδ κατέρχεται. Ταῦτα δ᾿ ἦν σύμβολα ὅτι τινὲς τοῦ γένους ὑμῶν εὑρεθήσονται τέκνα Ἀβραάμ, καὶ ἐν μερίδι τοῦ Χριστοῦ εὑρισκόμενοι, ἄλλοι δὲ τέκνα μὲν τοῦ Ἀβραάμ., ὡς ἡ ἄμμος δὲ ἡ ἐπὶ τὸ χεῖλος τῆς θαλάσσης ὄντες , ἥτις ἄγονός τε καὶ ἄκαρπος, πολλὴ μὲν καὶ ἀναρίθμητος ὑπάρχουσα, οὐδὲν δὲ ὅλως καρπογονοῦσα, ἀλλὰ μόνον τὸ ὕδωρ τῆς θαλάσσης πίνουσα· ὅπερ καὶ τὸ ἐν τῷ γένει ὑμῶν πολὺ πλῆθος ἐλέγχεται, πικρίας μὲν διδάγματα καὶ ἀθεότητος συμπίνοντες, τὸν δὲ τοῦ θεοῦ λόγον ἀποπτύοντες. Φησὶ γοῦν καὶ ἐν τῷ Ἰούδᾳ Οὑκ ἐκλείψει ἄρχων ἐξ Ἰούδα καὶ ἡγούμενος ἐκ τῶν μηρῶν αὐτοῦ, ἕως ἄν ἔλθῃ ᾧ ἀποκεῖται καὶ αὐτὸς ἔσται προσδοκία ἐθνῶν . Καὶ τοῦτο ὅτι οὐκ εἰς Ἰούδαν ἐρρέθη ἀλλ᾿ εἰς τὸν Χριστόν, φαίνεται· καὶ γὰρ Ἰούδαν πάντες οἱ ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν πάντων οὐ προσδοκῶμεν, ἀλλὰ Ἰησοῦν, τὸν καὶ τοὺς πατέρας ὑμῶν ἐξ Αἰγύπτου ἐξαγαγόντα. Μέχρι γὰρ τῆς παρουσίας τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἡ προφητεία προεκήρυσσεν· Ἕως ἂν ἔλθῃ ᾧ ἀπόκειται· καὶ αὐτὸς ἔσται προσδοκία ἐθνῶν. Ἐλήλυθε τοιγαροῦν, ὡς καὶ ἐν πολλοῖς ἀπεδείξαμεν, καὶ προσδοκᾶται πάλιν παρέσεσθαι ἐπάνω τῶν νεφελῶν Ἰησοῦς , οὗ τὸ ὄνομα βεβηλοῦτε ὑμεῖς καὶ βεβηλοῦσθαι ἐν πάσῃ τῇ γῇ ἐξεργάζεσθε. Δυνατὸν δὲ ἦν μοι, ἔφην, ὦ ἄνδρες, μάχεσθαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς περὶ τῆς λέξεως, ἣν ὑμεῖς ἐξηγεῖσθε λέγοντες εἰρῆσθαι· Ἕως ἂν ἔλθῃ τὰ ἀποκείμενα αὐτῷ· ἐπειδὴ οὐχ οὕτως ἐξηγήσαντο οἱ ἑβδομήκοντα, ἀλλ᾿· Ἕως ἂν ἔλθῃ ᾧ ἀπόκειται. Ἐπειδὴ δὲ τὰ ἀκόλουθα μηνύει ὅτι περὶ Χριστοῦ εἴρηται, οὕτω γὰρ ἔχουσι· Καὶ αὐτὸς ἔσται προσδοκία ἐθνῶν, οὐ περὶ τοῦ λεξειδίου συζητῆσαι ὑμῖν ἔρχομαι, ὅνπερ τρόπον οὐδὲ ἀπὸ τῶν μή ὁμολογουμένων ὑφ᾿ ὑμῶν γραφῶν, ὧν καὶ ἀνιστόρησα, ἀπὸ λόγων Ἱερεμίου τοῦ προφήτου καὶ Ἔσδρα καὶ Δαυΐδ, τὴν ἀπόδειξιν τήν περὶ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ποιήσασθαι ἐσπούδασα, ἀλλ᾿ ἀπὸ τῶν ὁμολογουμένων μέχρι νῦν ὑφ᾿ ὑμῶν· ἃ εἰ ἐνενοήκεισαν οἱ διδάσκαλοι ὑμῶν, εὖ ἴστε ὅτι ἀφανῆ ἐπεποιήκεισαν, ὡς καὶ τὰ περὶ τὸν θάνατον Ἡσαίου, ὃν πρίονι ξυλίνῳ ἐπρίσατε, μυστήριον καὶ αὐτὸ τοῦ Χριστοῦ, τοῦ τέμνειν ὑμῶν τὸ γένος διχῆ μέλλοντος, καὶ τοὺς μὲν ἀξίους σὺν τοῖς ἁγίοις πατριάρχαις καὶ προφήταις τῆς αἰωνίου βασιλείας καταξιοῦν μέλλοντος, τοὺς δὲ ἐπὶ τὴν καταδίκην τοῦ ἀσβέστου πυρὸς σὺν τοῖς ὁμοίοις ἀπειθέσι καὶ ἀμεταθέτοις ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν ἐθνῶν πέμψειν ἤδη φήσαντος. Ἥξουσι γάρ, εἶπεν, ἀπὸ δυσμῶν καὶ ἀνατολῶν, καὶ ἀνακλιθήσονται μετὰ Ἀβραὰμ καὶ Ἰσαὰκ καὶ Ἰακὼβ ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν οἱ δὲ υἱοὶ τῆς βασιλείας ἐκβληθήσονται εἰς τὸ σκότος τὸ ἐξώτερον . Καὶ ταῦτα, εἶπον, ὅτι οὐδὲν οὐδενὸς φροντίζω ἢ τοῦ τἀληθὲς λέγειν, λέγοιμι, οὐδένα δυσωπήσεσθαι μέλλων, κἂν δέῃ παραυτίκα ὑφ᾿ ὑμῶν μελισθῆναι. Οὐδὲ γὰρ ἀπὸ τοῦ γένους τοῦ ἐμοῦ, λέγω δὲ τῶν Σαμαρέων, τινὸς φροντίδα ποιούμενος, ἐγγράφως Καίσαρι προσομιλῶν, εἶπον πλανᾶσθαι αὐτοὺς πειθομένους τῷ ἐν τῷ γένει αὐτῶν μάγῳ Σίμωνι, ὃν θεὸν ὑπεράνω πάσης ἀρχῆς καὶ ἐξουσίας καὶ δυνάμεως εἶναι λέγουσι.
pass_a_gloss: You see, then, how He promises the same things to Isaac and to Jacob. For thus He says to Isaac: And all the nations of the earth will be blessed in your seed; and to Jacob: And all the tribes of the earth will be blessed in you and in your seed. He no longer says this to Esau or to Reuben or to any other person, but to those from whom the Christ was going to be according to the plan which is through the virgin Mary. For if you also consider the blessing of Judah, you will see what I say. For the seed is divided from Jacob, and through Judah and Phares and Jesse and David it comes down. But these things were symbols that some of your race will be found to be children of Abraham, and being in the portion of the Christ, others, however, are children of Abraham, but like the sand which is on the shore of the sea, which is barren and unfruitful, although it is numerous and countless, it produces no fruit at all, but only drinks the water of the sea; which is also what is condemned in the large multitude of your race, drinking the teachings of bitterness and atheism, and spitting out the word of God. For it is said, indeed, in Judah: A ruler will not fail from Judah, and a leader from his thighs, until what is reserved for him comes, and he will be the expectation of the nations. And that this was not said about Judah but about the Christ is clear; for we do not expect Judah, all of us from all the nations, but Jesus, who also led your fathers out of Egypt. For until the coming of the Christ, the prophecy was preached: Until what is reserved for him comes, and he will be the expectation of the nations. Therefore, he has come, as we have shown in many ways, and is expected to come again on the clouds, Jesus, whose name you profane and strive to profane in all the earth. But it was possible for me to fight with you about the phrase which you interpret, saying it was said: Until what is reserved for him comes; since the seventy did not interpret it thus, but: Until he comes to whom it is reserved. And since the following words indicate that it was said about the Christ, for they have: And he will be the expectation of the nations, I do not come to argue with you about the phrase, nor from the writings which you do not acknowledge, from which I also produced the proof about the Christ, from the words of the prophet Jeremiah and Ezra and David, but from those which are acknowledged by you up to now; which if your teachers had understood, you know that they would have made them obscure, as also the things about the death of Isaiah, whom you sawed in half with a wooden saw, a mystery also of the Christ, who is going to divide your race in two, and is going to deem some worthy to be with the holy patriarchs and prophets in the eternal kingdom, but others to be sent to the judgment of unquenchable fire with those who are similar and disobedient and unrepentant from all the nations, as he has already said. For they will come, he said, from the west and the east, and will recline with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven, but the sons of the kingdom will be cast out into the outer darkness. And I said these things because I care about nothing except telling the truth, and I am not going to flatter anyone, even if I must be hated by you right now. For I am not concerned about my own race, I mean the Samaritans, speaking to Caesar in writing, I said that they are deceived, believing in the magician Simon who is in their race, whom they say is a god above all authority and power and might.

A ruler will not fail from Judah, and a leader from his thighs

pass_b_english: Notice how God promises the same things to Isaac and to Jacob. To Isaac He says, "All the nations of the earth will be blessed in your seed" (Gen 28:14); to Jacob, "All the tribes of the earth will be blessed in you and in your seed" (Gen 28:14). He no longer says this to Esau, or to Reuben, or to anyone else, but only to those from whom the Christ was to come according to the plan worked through the virgin Mary. If you would only examine the blessing of Judah, you would see what I mean. The line of descent divides from Jacob and runs through Judah, Perez, Jesse, and David. These genealogies were symbols showing that some of your race will be found to be true children of Abraham, standing in the portion of the Christ, while others, though children of Abraham, are like the sand on the seashore: barren and unfruitful, vast and innumerable, yet producing nothing at all — only drinking the seawater. That is exactly what condemns the vast multitude of your people: you drink the teachings of bitterness and atheism, and spit out the word of God.

Scripture indeed says in Judah: "A ruler will not fail from Judah, and a leader from his loins, until he comes to whom it belongs, and he will be the expectation of the nations" (Gen 49:10). It is clear this was spoken not of Judah but of the Christ. We from all nations do not wait for Judah; we wait for Jesus, the one who led your fathers out of Egypt. Until the Christ's coming the prophecy was proclaimed: "Until he comes to whom it belongs, and he will be the expectation of the nations." He has come, as we have shown in many ways, and He is expected to come again on the clouds — Jesus, whose name you profane and strive to profane throughout the earth. I could dispute the phrase with you — you read it, "Until what is reserved for him comes" — but the Seventy did not translate it that way; they rendered it, "Until he comes to whom it is reserved." Since the following words — "And he will be the expectation of the nations" — show the passage concerns the Christ, I will not wrangle over a single phrase, nor appeal to writings you reject (Jeremiah, Ezra, David), from which I have also drawn proof. I argue from the Scriptures you yourselves acknowledge up to this day. If your teachers had understood them, you know they would have suppressed them, just as they did the account of Isaiah's death — you sawed him in half with a wooden saw — which is itself a mystery of the Christ who will divide your race in two: some He will deem worthy to recline with the holy patriarchs and prophets in the eternal kingdom; others He will send to the judgment of unquenchable fire alongside the disobedient and unrepentant from every nation, as He has already declared: "They will come from east and west and recline with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven, but the sons of the kingdom will be cast into the outer darkness." I say these things because I care for nothing but the truth; I will not flatter anyone, even if you hate me for it this very moment. I am not defending my own race — I mean the Samaritans — for in a written address to Caesar I charged them with being deceived by the magician Simon of their own people, whom they call a god above all authority, power, and might.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text of Dialogue 120. Pass A provides a literal rendering, while Pass B provides a fluent rendering with appropriate scripture citations (Genesis 28:14, Genesis 49:10) that match the quoted content. All nuances regarding the 'plan' (οἰκονομία), the 'seventy' (ἑβδομήκοντα), and the 'magician Simon' (μάγῳ Σίμωνι) are preserved.
source: [p1], English: 'You see, then, how He promises the same things to Isaac and to Jacob.'
